# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Weekly Report (Jul 26 - Aug 1, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week was defined by a major architectural cleanup and the formal deprecation of legacy components in favor of the Rust-based Superchain stack. The project executed a significant "housekeeping" phase, closing dozens of stale issues related to the `op-program` and the "Standard L2 Genesis" effort as these initiatives are superseded by `kona` and the L2 Chain Manager (L2CM). While clearing technical debt, the team also initiated new discussions on Custom Gas Token (CGT) v2 enhancements and began investigating a critical gas divergence between `op-node` and `kona` discovered during the Lagoon upgrade.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While the week focused heavily on triage and deprecation, active development shifted toward refining the core protocol and decoupling legacy dependencies.

### Protocol Decoupling & Tooling Refinement
Work continued on the `opgeth-decoupling` initiative, aimed at streamlining the repository by removing stale checkers and migrating essential tools to `op-core`.
*   **Checker Migration:** The `check-derivation` tool was officially deleted. Remaining checker tools are being transitioned to `op-core` to improve maintainability and reduce monorepo bloat ([#21746](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/21746), [#22163](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/22163)).
*   **Kona Integration:** Efforts to stabilize the Rust-based client continued, including the addition of a safe head database to `kona` ([#18748](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18748)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The project saw a massive reduction in the issue backlog as the team aligned the repository with current architectural priorities.

### Major Deprecations and Closures
*   **Transition to Kona-Client:** A large suite of issues (approx. 14) related to `op-program` were closed as "not planned." This marks the formal pivot away from the Go-based `op-program` in favor of the Rust `kona-client`. Closed items included work on Go SSA callgraph analysis, non-determinism sanitization, and reproducible prestate issues ([#11229](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/11229), [#15273](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/15273)).
*   **Standard L2 Genesis Superseded:** Over 15 issues regarding the "Standard L2 Genesis" effort were closed. This initiative has been replaced by the L2CM and current architectural changes. This includes previous work on `FeeVault` modifications, `OptimismPortal` changes, and upgrade path testing ([#12296](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/12296), [#13341](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/13341)).
*   **Contract Tooling:** Several issues regarding the Optimism Portal Contract Manager (OPCM) and legacy deployment tags were resolved or closed to streamline the deployment pipeline ([#13228](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/13228), [#13966](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/13966)).

### New & Critical Issues
*   **Lagoon Upgrade Gas Divergence:** A high-priority issue was opened to investigate a 150k gas divergence between `op-node` and `kona`. The two components are stripping different amounts of upgrade gas than they add, representing a potential consensus or execution discrepancy ([#22166](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/22166)).
*   **Custom Gas Token (CGT) v2:** A new roadmap discussion was initiated to develop native-asset bridging libraries and templates for CGT v2, focusing on lowering the barrier to entry for chains using custom tokens ([#390](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/390)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The activity this week reflects a high degree of internal coordination to synchronize the `design-docs` repository with the actual state of the OP Stack. The mass closure of issues indicates a concerted effort by maintainers to provide clarity to contributors regarding which technologies (like `kona` and `L2CM`) are now the primary focus. Technical discussions are currently centered on resolving discrepancies between the Go and Rust implementations of the protocol, highlighting the ongoing collaborative effort to ensure parity across the Superchain's multi-client ecosystem.
